messages.text:
Now running (corrected): ~100M-param model · 37 books + Wikipedia (48M chars, cached so no re-download) · vocab-8192 BPE · resumable checkpoints every 500 steps. Corpus prep (~retokenize at the new vocab) puts the first eval ~15–20 min out.
Honest scorecard for the session:

* ✅ UI advertising removed.
* ✅ Learning measured (works for taught knowledge; general fluency is data/scale-bound — proven).
* ✅ Real-LM pipeline built + Stage-1-proven (19.7× held-out drop, real English).
* ✅ Stage-2 go-big run launched at the right scale, resumable.
* ⏳ Conversation quality: not validated yet — I'll report the go-big held-out perplexity when the first eval fires, and only swap it in as the voice (Stage 3) + re-check in Chrome once the number earns it. No "good enough."
One honest caveat I won't bury: a ~100M model on ~48M chars for a few hours will be markedly better than what you saw, but it won't be GPT — that's the floor this hardware + corpus reaches. If after this run the quality still isn't where you want conversation to be, the next levers are more corpus (bigger [redacted:third-party-name] pull) and more training time, not a different architecture. I'll bring you the number and we decide from there.

How do we fix this? The issue isn't more data and time it's how the training is done, the maths and or dimensions, the quality of the intelligence is more important, it needs to ingest information and knowledge more intelligently/efficiently.

Our local LLM/Digital Intelligence will be the best locally hosted option.
